title: Managing product delivery: practices applied and judging the process
blurb: Name the practice a team manager's action applies in managing product delivery, and judge whether the team manager is handling the work package effectively.
question: A supplier's project engineer is asked by a board member to move an installation date, agrees, and reschedules without telling the project manager. Is the work package being handled effectively, and why?

teach.h: Two question types on managing product delivery
teach.body: Practitioner papers ask which practice a delivery action applies, using table 17.3; the official extracts examiners quote link managing product delivery to quality, plans, issues and progress. They also ask whether the team manager's handling of a work package is effective. Judge that against the recommended actions in 17.4 and the objectives in 17.2, then choose the reason that explains this situation.

teach.h: How managing product delivery applies the practices
head: Practice
What the team manager does (table 17.3)
rows: Develops the specialist products; updates the quality register
Develops the team plan; updates the product register
Applies the agreed way of handling issues within the work package; issue register updated via the PM
teach.caption: Paraphrased from the official extracts quoted in sample rationales. Four practices, four simple anchors.

root.label: What did the team manager produce or update?

teach.caption: A failed test result goes in the quality register (quality); raising the problem with the PM as the WPD requires applies issues.

teach.h: How to judge the team manager
teach.body: Managing product delivery works when the team's work is authorized and agreed, the team is clear on what it is producing and the expected effort, cost and timescales, products are delivered to the quality expected and within tolerance, and the PM gets accurate progress information at the agreed frequency. Test each action against those objectives and the recommended actions, then weigh the scenario facts.

rows.label: New issues, risks
values: Kept in the team or hidden

rows.label: Reporting
values: Checkpoints to the PM as agreed

steps.label:
Raise an issue
to the PM

teach.caption: The team manager works within work package tolerances and escalates a forecast breach to the PM, never past the PM.

teach.h: A design work package in two-week cycles

items.label: Accept the WP; team plan by cycle

teach.caption: An iterative supplier fits managing product delivery: the cycles sit inside one agreed work package.

teach.body: For the Fernhollow Kitchen launch, design agency account director Felix Haddad accepts a packaging work package from project manager Nadia Osei. He plans the agency's two-week cycles in a team plan (plans), records tasting and recyclability test results in the quality register (quality), sends Nadia a checkpoint report after each cycle (progress) and, when a sleeve ink fails the kerbside recyclability check, raises it with Nadia as the work package requires (issues). Each action is effective because it meets an MP objective.

teach.text: Traps: (1) A failed quality test is recorded in the quality register, but the PROBLEM is raised with the PM: the team manager does not grant concessions or rewrite specifications. (2) Team managers produce checkpoint reports for the PM, not highlight reports for the board. (3) A board member's request to a team manager is not an instruction: work comes through the PM. (4) The team plan is optional; a supplier does not need to use PRINCE2.

items: Table 17.3: quality (products, quality register), plans (team plan, product register), issues (handle issues as agreed), progress (checkpoint reports).
Judge against 17.2: agreed work, clear expectations, quality within tolerance, accurate progress to the PM.
The team manager takes action required by the PM, not by board members.
A forecast work package breach goes to the PM as an issue.

summary: You can now name the practice behind any managing product delivery action using table 17.3. You can also judge a team manager's handling of a work package against the MP objectives and pick the reason that explains it.

A.q: Fernhollow Foods is launching Fernhollow Kitchen. Gerrit Vos, project engineer at the Dutch line supplier, prepares a team plan for installing and commissioning the tray-sealing line during the factory shutdown, and updates the product register entries for the line's products. Which practice is the 'managing product delivery' process applying?
options: Quality
Progress
Plans
Issues
A.why: Table 17.3 links managing product delivery to the plans practice through developing the team plan and updating the product register.

whyNot.0: Quality is applied by developing the specialist products and updating the quality register.
whyNot.1: Progress is applied through checkpoint reports.
whyNot.3: Issues is applied by handling issues within the work package as agreed.

A.q: On the Fernhollow Kitchen project, Megan Cho's chefs complete shelf-life tests on four recipes under their work package, and Megan records the results in the quality register. Which practice is the 'managing product delivery' process applying?
options: Quality
Plans
Progress
Issues
A.why: Table 17.3: the quality practice is applied when the team develops the specialist products and updates the quality register.

whyNot.1: Plans is applied through the team plan and the product register, not test results.
whyNot.2: Progress is applied through checkpoint reports to the PM.
whyNot.3: No problem is being raised here; the action is recording quality results.

A.q: Felix Haddad of the design agency Mint and Tallow sends project manager Nadia Osei a report on the status of the packaging design work package at the end of each two-week cycle, as agreed when he accepted it. Which practice is the 'managing product delivery' process applying?
options: Organizing
Plans
Issues
Progress
A.why: Table 17.3: the progress practice is applied in managing product delivery by developing checkpoint reports.

whyNot.0: Organizing concerns roles and structure; it is not the practice table 17.3 links to checkpoint reports.
whyNot.1: Plans is applied through the team plan and product register.
whyNot.2: Issues is applied when problems are handled as the work package requires.

B.q: During the packaging work package for Fernhollow Kitchen, a sleeve ink fails the kerbside recyclability check. Felix Haddad follows the work package's procedure and raises the problem with Nadia Osei so it can be recorded in the issue register, rather than changing the specification himself. Which practice is the 'managing product delivery' process applying?
options: Quality
Issues
Plans
Progress
B.why: Table 17.3: the issues practice is applied by handling issues within the work package as agreed and updating the issue register via the PM.

whyNot.0: The failed check is a quality result, but raising the problem through the agreed route applies the issues practice.
whyNot.2: Plans is applied through the team plan and product register.
whyNot.3: Progress is applied through checkpoint reports; this is a specific problem being raised.

B.q: Gerrit Vos forecasts that a shipping delay will push installation of the new line beyond his work package's time tolerance by a week. The Fernhollow Kitchen stage plan may still absorb it. What should Gerrit do?
options: Raise it with Nadia Osei as an issue
Send an exception report to the project board
Agree a new date with the operations director
Extend his team plan and carry on
B.why: Team managers work within work package tolerances and escalate a forecast breach to the PM as an issue; the PM then decides in controlling a stage (11.2.1, 17.4.2).

whyNot.1: Exception reports go from the PM to the board for forecast stage or project breaches; the team manager reports to the PM.
whyNot.2: The operations director is not the team manager's route for changes to the work package; the team manager takes action required by the PM.
whyNot.3: A forecast breach of tolerance cannot be absorbed silently; it must be raised with the PM.

B.q: Felix Haddad sends his fortnightly checkpoint reports for the packaging work package to Charlotte Vane, the sales and marketing director on the project board, because she owns the brand. He copies nobody else. Which statement best explains why this is not effective?
options: Checkpoint reports should be monthly, not fortnightly
Felix should report to the executive, not to Charlotte
Checkpoint reports go to the PM at the agreed frequency
Charlotte should receive highlight reports from Felix
B.why: An MP objective is accurate progress information to the PM at an agreed frequency; checkpoint reports go from the team manager to the PM (17.2, 17.4.2).

whyNot.0: The frequency is whatever the work package agreed; fortnightly is not the problem.
whyNot.1: The board, including the executive, is not involved in MP; the report should go to the PM.
whyNot.3: Highlight reports are produced by the PM for the board, not by team managers.

C.q: Dariusz Nowicki, Fernhollow's operations director and a project board member, phones Gerrit Vos and asks him to move the line installation until after the Christmas peak. Gerrit agrees and reschedules his team without telling Nadia Osei. Is Gerrit handling the work package effectively, and why?
options: Yes, because Dariusz will own the line and knows the factory peak
Yes, because the team plan is the team manager's to change
No, because the team manager should act on the PM's instructions
No, because the change should be approved by the senior supplier
C.why: In execute a work package, the team manager notifies the PM of new issues and takes any action required by the PM, not directly by board members (17.4.2). The board is not involved in MP.

whyNot.0: Dariusz's knowledge is relevant, but his request must go through the PM, who can assess its impact on the launch date.
whyNot.1: The team plan is the team manager's, but moving a work package milestone changes the agreed work and needs the PM.
whyNot.3: Whoever might later approve the change, the team manager must first refer it to the PM; a senior supplier's approval would not replace that.

C.q: One of the Fernhollow Kitchen recipes fails the eight-day shelf-life test. Megan Cho records the failed result in the quality register, notifies Nadia Osei of the issue, and carries on with the other recipes in her team plan. Is this an appropriate application of 'execute a work package', and why?
options: Yes, because the team manager can grant a concession for the recipe
Yes, because she notifies the PM and updates the quality register
No, because the team manager should raise an exception report
No, because failed test results belong in the daily log instead
C.why: Execute a work package includes notifying the PM of new issues, risks or lessons and updating the quality register with completed quality activities (17.4.2).

whyNot.0: Concessions for off-specifications are decided by the board or a change authority, not the team manager.
whyNot.2: Exception reports are the PM's route to the board; the team manager notifies the PM.
whyNot.3: Results of quality activities are recorded in the quality register; the daily log is the PM's informal diary.

C.q: Felix Haddad accepts the packaging design work package without writing a separate team plan, because the agency's two-week cycles and tasting dates are already set out in the work package. Nadia Osei agrees. Is this an appropriate application of 'accept a work package', and why?
options: Yes, because the stage plan already sets out the agency's cycles
Yes, because a team plan is optional when accepting a work package
No, because a team manager must produce a team plan for each package
No, because the agency must plan its work using PRINCE2 products
C.why: Team plans are optional in PRINCE2; in accept a work package what matters is that the work is agreed and achievable (17.4.1).

whyNot.0: The verdict is right, but the stage plan is the PM's plan for the whole stage; it is not why a team plan can be skipped.
whyNot.2: The team plan is optional, so its absence is not a failing.
whyNot.3: Suppliers do not need to use PRINCE2; an agency can plan in its own cycles.

reteach.title: One work package, four practices
reteach.question: Follow a single work package from start to finish. Which practice is at work at each point?

blocks.body: At the start the team manager may write a team plan and keeps the product register current: plans. While building, the team develops products and records quality activities in the quality register: quality. When something goes wrong, the team handles it as the work package says and raises it with the PM: issues. Throughout, the team sends checkpoint reports to the PM: progress.

blocks.text: Effective means following the PM's direction, raising new issues and risks to the PM and reporting at the agreed frequency. Taking orders from a board member is not effective, however senior they are.

explain.body: Quality: the team develops the specialist products and updates the quality register. Plans: the team manager develops the team plan when one is needed and updates the product register.

test.q: Megan Cho updates the product register entry for each Fernhollow Kitchen recipe as it moves from draft to ready for factory trials. Which practice does table 17.3 link this action to?
options: Quality
Plans
Progress
Business case
test.why: Table 17.3 lists updating the product register, with developing the team plan, under the plans practice in managing product delivery.

whyNot.0: Quality is linked to the quality register and developing products, not the product register.
whyNot.2: Progress is linked to checkpoint reports.
whyNot.3: The business case is not one of the practices table 17.3 links to this action.

explain.body: Issues: the team handles issues within the work package in the way the work package sets out, and the issue register is updated through the PM. Progress: the team manager develops checkpoint reports for the PM.

test.q: Gerrit Vos's team finds a minor wiring fault during commissioning. Gerrit handles it using the procedure set out in his work package and passes the details to Nadia Osei for the issue register. Which practice is the 'managing product delivery' process applying?
options: Progress
Quality
Issues
Risk
test.why: Table 17.3: the issues practice is applied when issues within the work package are handled as agreed and the issue register is updated via the PM.

whyNot.0: Progress is applied through checkpoint reports, not through handling a specific fault.
whyNot.1: The fault affects a product, but handling it through the agreed issue procedure applies issues.
whyNot.3: The fault has already happened, so it is an issue, not a risk.

explain.h: Judging how work is taken on and done
explain.body: Effective team managers agree the work package before starting, check it is achievable, take direction from the PM, and notify the PM of new issues, risks and lessons. Ineffective ones start on assumptions, accept impossible work or follow instructions from elsewhere.

test.q: Nadia Osei wants every team on Fernhollow Kitchen to be clear on what it is producing and the expected effort, cost and timescales. Which team manager action best meets that managing product delivery objective?
options: Agreeing the work package with the PM before work starts
Sending checkpoint reports to a board member each week
Taking direction from the operations director on dates
Skipping the achievability check to start work sooner
test.why: Agreeing the work package before work starts, in accept a work package, is how the team becomes clear on what is to be produced and the expected effort, cost and timescales (17.2, 17.4.1).

whyNot.1: Checkpoint reports go to the PM; sending them to a board member does not clarify the team's work.
whyNot.2: Direction comes from the PM; a board member's instruction bypasses the agreed work package.
whyNot.3: Checking whether the work is achievable is part of accepting a work package.

explain.body: The PM needs accurate progress information at the agreed frequency. A checkpoint report that hides a known risk, or goes to the wrong person, fails that objective even if it is on time.

children.edge: Accurate, to the PM, on time
children.label: Effective

test.q: Gerrit Vos's checkpoint report says commissioning is on track. He leaves out a new risk that his firm's engineers may be unavailable during the factory shutdown, so as not to worry Nadia Osei. Is his reporting effective, and why?
options: Yes, because the checkpoint reports the work package status
Yes, because risks are reported by the PM in highlight reports
No, because the risk should go to the board as an exception
No, because new risks should be notified to the project manager
test.why: In execute a work package the team manager notifies the PM of any new issues, risks or lessons, so the PM has accurate information (17.2, 17.4.2).

whyNot.0: Reporting status is part of the job, but leaving out a known risk makes the information inaccurate.
whyNot.1: The PM does report to the board, but can only do so if the team manager passes the risk on.
whyNot.2: A new risk goes to the PM, who decides whether stage tolerance is threatened; the team manager does not escalate to the board.
